clue.text: Head takes in a classical subject in the count's domain

indicators.note: the head swallows the next words, so they go inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
Latin is the classical language studied at school

explanation.surface: A headmaster introduces a classical subject in a nobleman's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader; it is the top of the skull. A count palatine ruled a territory with royal powers.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatinate is the territory ruled by a count palatine, a noble with near-royal powers.

clue.text: Perform song with piano introduction

indicators.note: the piano comes in first, ahead of the song

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: Sing a number after a short piano opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to perform music or a part on stage.

clue.text: Do small hand-outs like this one grow on trees?

definitions.text: Do small hand-outs like this one grow on trees?

parts.words: Do small hand-outs like this one grow on trees?
parts.note: plays on a printed handbill and on the little leaf of a compound leaf, which does grow on a tree

explanation.surface: Wondering whether free handbills are as plentiful as leaves on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handbill is distributed free, and a small leaf or division of a compound leaf grows on a tree.

clue.text: Job for a Dickensian going round Spain perhaps, checking rail transport

indicators.note: the Dickens character surrounds the jumbled country

parts.note: Job Trotter is Mr Jingle's servant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

indicators.note: suggests the country's name could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A Dickens character travels around Spain inspecting the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work; it is the first name of a servant in Pickwick Papers. 'perhaps' scrambles the country, which 'going round' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist who notes locomotive numbers spends time watching and logging trains.

clue.text: Where wicked madmen go? Must be crackers to break into it

definitions.text: Must be crackers to break into it

parts.note: nuts is slang for lunatics
the place where the wicked are sent is damnation's pit

explanation.surface: Asking where crazed sinners end up, and saying you'd be mad to break in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' means mad on the surface, but it is nutcrackers breaking the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcrackers are needed to break the hard case around a kernel.

clue.text: Doctor catches fish in arctic region? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: on the surface the doctor takes in the fish
swaps the roles, so the fish holds the doctor inside

parts.note: tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: A medic lands a fish in polar waters, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' says the surface's capture runs the other way: the fish catches the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless frozen plain of the far north.

clue.text: Authentication is required to enter the state

indicators.note: the word is must go into the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Proof of identity is needed before you can come into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement in a passport, a form of authentication for travel.

clue.text: First thing to do to an alteration

definitions.text: thing to do to an alteration

explanation.surface: The first step in making a change is to sign it off.
explanation.definitionFit: First means at the beginning; one also writes one's initials beside a correction to authorise it.

clue.text: Martin Tate contrived to make this hypothetical stuff

indicators.note: devised artificially, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Martin Tate came up with a theoretical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter of opposite charge to ordinary matter, once only theoretical, is the stuff described.

clue.text: After 25 queen holds it the wrong way (very hard)

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the answer to 25, which leads

parts.note: the answer to 25 down is the first gardener, Eden's man

indicators.note: the queen's name contains the next piece inside it

parts.note: Anne was a queen of England

indicators.note: the word it is read backwards before going in

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by a queen holding something backwards, all very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' points to 25 down; 'the wrong way' turns the little word before 'holds' puts it inside the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine describes something unbreakable, like the legendary hardest stone, so very hard is a synonym.

clue.text: Part of 12-member's outfit going round the lake (or loch, rather?)

indicators.note: the outfit encircles the lake, so its letters surround it

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing or gear
L is the standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A Highlander's garment wraps around a body of water, which a Scot would call a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is CLAN, so a 12-member is a clansman. The bracket jokes that a Scot would say loch, but L still serves.
explanation.definitionFit: The tartan skirt is the best-known garment of a Scottish clansman's dress.

clue.text: Former Soviet minister, one at : the food supply department

parts.note: a commissar headed a government department in the Soviet Union
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Soviet official is posted to the department in charge of rations.
explanation.definitionFit: An army's commissariat is the branch providing food and stores.

clue.text: See 10

annotationWithheld.why: The clue as held is only 'See 10'; no group links 12 to 10, and CLAN is merely implied by '12-member' in 10's clue, with no wordplay of its own.

clue.text: One headless form, human, this instrument creates

indicators.note: the pieces are made into something new, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the word form loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone without a head, in human form, makes this musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' leaves ORM from form; with I and HUMAN that gives nine letters, which 'creates' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is a small reed organ worked by pedals, a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Bill, with French horn, is on the ball, showing conformity

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
cor is the French word for horn
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill plays a French horn at a dance, keeping in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like the instrument; it is the French word for horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Accordance is agreement or harmony with a rule, as in 'in accordance with'.

clue.text: Old war engine 'or modern aeroplane launcher

explanation.surface: A siege weapon of old is also used to fire planes off carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient siege engine hurled stones; the same name is used for the steam device launching aircraft from a carrier deck.

clue.text: Tea round, the chimney retreat that works like a charm

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the tea goes around the chimney, containing it

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A cup of tea by the fireside is a comforting retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sets the chimney inside the drink; 'retreat' turns the whole back to front. The chimney word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a talisman worn for protection, an object believed to have magical power.

clue.text: Could the rat race be called, like Kipling's book, Life's —?

definitions.text: Could the rat race be called, like Kipling's book, Life's —?

parts.words: Could the rat race be called, like Kipling's book, Life's —?
parts.note: Kipling's 1891 story collection title is completed, and the word also names a race where runners carry weights

explanation.surface: Wondering if the daily grind is a burden, as a Kipling title says.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage imposed on stronger competitors, and a race run under such conditions; Kipling's book is Life's Handicap.

clue.text: Old boy' recently became a dedicated type

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
lately or late means not long ago

explanation.surface: A former pupil has lately become a devoted sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: An OLD BOY is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a person dedicated to religious life, often a lay member attached to a monastery.

clue.text: Naval battle for the French Christmas show

parts.note: le is French for the
panto, a pantomime, is a British comic stage show put on at Christmas

explanation.surface: A naval battle is staged as a French festive play.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is a British family stage show staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was the 1571 sea fight in which the Holy League defeated the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: In which recorded material is fixed between players say

indicators.note: the fixed part sits inside the word for the players
signals a word that sounds like the cast of a play

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a production
set means fixed or settled

explanation.surface: Recorded material has been firmly placed between some actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns the players into a sound-alike word for a social class; 'between' sets the fixed piece inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cartridge holds recorded sound or video, so it is where recordings are kept.

clue.text: Call it the end of the wood destroyer

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Calling time on a pest that ruins timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are insects that eat through timber, ruining woodwork.

clue.text: Attack makes. Balaam's mount unwell

parts.note: in the Bible Balaam rode an ass, which spoke to him
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Balaam's donkey is sick and lashes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, with blows or words.

clue.text: Glum appearance of the fourth estate indeed

indicators.note: the press makes an appearance inside the deed, so it goes in

parts.note: read as in deed, a deed being an act
the fourth estate is a traditional name for the newspapers

explanation.surface: A gloomy look on journalists' faces, certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'indeed' as 'in deed': the newspapers appear inside the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or dejected, as a glum person is.

clue.text: A measure of old port

explanation.surface: A unit of size belongs to an ancient harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land area is the first sense; Acre is also an ancient port city in present-day Israel.

clue.text: Gardener with a beastly mother? He had 26

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Did the first gardener have an animal for a mother? He had none at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail says the first man had no mother, 26 being NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man was put in Eden to tend it, so he is the first gardener.

clue.text: Not one who begat Joshua, we hear

indicators.note: the father's name is spoken, and what is heard is the answer

parts.note: the Bible calls Joshua the son of Nun

explanation.surface: Asking about someone who was not the father of Joshua, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a single one, nobody at all.

clue.text: "Spitting from lips once ____ by Hers" (Browning to Fitzgerald)

definitions.text: "Spitting from lips once ____ by Hers" (Browning to Fitzgerald)

parts.words: "Spitting from lips once ____ by Hers" (Browning to Fitzgerald)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the last line of Robert Browning's angry sonnet to Edward FitzGerald, who had written slightingly of Elizabeth Barrett Browning

explanation.surface: A line from a poet's furious rebuke, with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's line says lips made holy by his late wife's kisses would spit on FitzGerald.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means made holy, consecrated by her kisses.

clue.text: Love comes to a pachyderm in the end

indicators.note: only the closing stretch of the animal's name is kept

parts.note: the rhinoceros is a thick-skinned pachyderm

explanation.surface: Romance arrives for an elephant at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the last four letters of RHINOCEROS, a classic pachyderm.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, so the name stands for love itself.

clue.text: Mistake by master floundering in the pilot's wake

parts.note: a slip is a small error

indicators.note: struggling in confusion, so the letters of master are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship's master errs and flounders behind the pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' scrambles the ship's master into a current of water, which follows the error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipstream is the current of air or water behind a moving craft, its trailing wake.
